started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are asking about Child Benefit for 1 child:
  - Alex is 15 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 15 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - No other claimant who lives with the child has priority
  - Child is in local authority care for 12 weeks
  - Child has been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks, but it is unknown how many hours per week child spends at home. It could be anywhere from zero to 100 hours
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to ask you about your child. 

**First, let's determine your child's age:**

The eligibility requirements differ based on the child's age:
- Children **under 16** may automatically qualify
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** generally don't qualify

**How old is your child?**

(If you have multiple children, we can check each one - let's start with one child first)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 15 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for that information. Let me check the eligibility for Alex, who is 15 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is 15 (under 16), this is a positive start. Now I need to check a few more requirements.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

This is important because children working 24 or more hours per week (who aren't in approved education/training) don't qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. Just focused on school at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about benefits:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking if Alex is receiving benefits like:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

in their own name (not yours). Most 15-year-olds don't receive these benefits, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't get any benefits in their own name. Nothing like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now let me ask about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

This matters because certain types of apprenticeships can affect eligibility:
- In **England**: All apprenticeships (Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, Degree) disqualify from Child Benefit
- In **Scotland**: Modern Apprenticeships disqualify
- In **Wales**: Foundation Apprenticeships are approved (don't disqualify), but other apprenticeships do disqualify

Since you mentioned Alex is in school, I'm guessing they're not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship. Just at school like I said.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about **your residency status** (as the claimant).

**Do you meet UK residency requirements?**

You qualify if **ANY** of the following apply to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (most common)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above National Insurance threshold)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Which of these applies to you?** (For most people, it's simply that they normally live in the UK)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check about your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You qualify if **ANY** of these apply:

1. **You live with Alex** (most common)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep by paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards their care - this includes things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement that equals or exceeds Child Benefit payments

**Do any of these apply to you?** (I'm assuming you live with Alex?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to ask about other claimants:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child. This is important if, for example:
- Alex's other parent is claiming
- A grandparent or other family member is claiming
- You share care with someone else

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex right now?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about Alex's living situation:

**Which of these describes Alex's current situation?**

- Alex is **in hospital** (for an extended period)
- Alex is **in care** (looked after by the local authority)
- Alex is **fostered**
- Alex is **living normally** at home with you

Based on what you've told me (Alex lives at home with you and is at school), I'm assuming it's "living normally" - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex has been in local authority care for a few months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I see, thank you for clarifying that. This is important information as it affects eligibility. Let me check the rules for children in local authority care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. When a child is in local authority care, there are specific time limits that apply.

**Important question: Has Alex been in care for 8 weeks or less, OR does Alex spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you?**

Here's how it works:
- Child Benefit continues for up to **8 weeks** when a child first goes into care
- You can also continue claiming if Alex spends **24 or more hours per week** at home with you
- You can claim again if Alex spends 2 consecutive nights per week OR 7+ days in a row at home

You mentioned Alex has been in care for "a few months" - can you tell me:
1. How long exactly has Alex been in care?
2. Does Alex spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been in care for about 12 weeks now. As for how much time they spend at home... I'm not entirely sure of the exact hours per week. Some weeks it varies quite a bit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex has been in care for about 12 weeks (which is more than 8 weeks), the key question is whether Alex regularly spends at least 24 hours per week at home with you.

Let me help you figure this out:

**Think about a typical week - does Alex spend at least 24 hours at home with you?**

For example:
- Does Alex come home for weekends? (2 nights would typically be more than 24 hours)
- Does Alex spend one or more full days at home each week?
- Are there regular overnight stays?

The rules say you can continue claiming if Alex spends:
- **2 consecutive nights per week** at home, OR
- **7 or more days in a row** at home

Even if the exact hours vary week to week, do either of these patterns generally apply? Does Alex typically spend at least 2 nights in a row at home each week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's the thing - it really does vary. Some weeks Alex comes home more, some weeks less. I honestly can't say for certain whether it consistently adds up to 24 hours a week or not. It might be, but I'm just not sure.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that's a tricky situation when the time varies week to week. Given the uncertainty about whether Alex consistently spends 24+ hours per week at home, and that Alex has been in care for more than 8 weeks, I need to give you an honest assessment.

Based on the rules in the Child Benefit specification:

**The situation is INDETERMINATE** - meaning I cannot definitively determine your eligibility based on the information available.

Here's why:
- Alex has been in care for approximately 12 weeks (more than the 8-week limit)
- You're uncertain whether Alex consistently spends 24+ hours per week at home
- The varying schedule makes it unclear if you meet the exception criteria

**What you should do:**

You'll need to **contact HMRC directly** to discuss your specific situation. They can:
- Review your exact circumstances in detail
- Help you calculate whether the time Alex spends at home meets the 24-hour threshold
- Consider the pattern of visits over recent weeks
- Make an official determination on your eligibility

**Contact HMRC Child Benefit Office:**
- Phone: 0300 200 3100
- Online: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-for-children-in-hospital-or-care

They'll be able to look at your individual case and give you a definitive answer. It's worth calling them, especially if some weeks Alex does come home for substantial periods.

Would you like me to provide you with this assessment summary?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see. Yes, that makes sense - I suppose I'll need to speak to HMRC directly to work out the exact hours. Thanks for your help in going through everything with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help you understand the process and identify what needs to be clarified with HMRC.

Let me provide you with a formal assessment summary now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Assessment Summary for Alex:**

✓ **Positive factors:**
- Alex is 15 years old (under 16) - meets age requirement
- Not working full-time
- Not receiving benefits in their own right
- Not in an apprenticeship
- You live in the UK and meet residency requirements
- You're responsible for Alex
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

⚠️ **Area requiring HMRC review:**
- Alex has been in local authority care for approximately 12 weeks (more than the 8-week limit)
- Uncertainty about whether Alex consistently spends 24+ hours per week at home (the key exception)

**Next Steps:**
Contact HMRC Child Benefit Office to discuss your specific situation:
- **Phone:** 0300 200 3100 (Monday to Friday, 8am to 6pm)
- **Online:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-for-children-in-hospital-or-care

When you call, be ready to explain the pattern of Alex's visits home - they can help you determine if it meets the requirements.

Best of luck with your call to HMRC, and I hope everything works out for you and Alex!
